business_problem: Cathay Pacific needed to replace paper-heavy flight operations with a digital, offline-capable system that could synchronize urgent updates, flight data, and collaboration across crews within a one-year delivery window.
solution_summary: Cathay Pacific built Flight Folder on MongoDB Atlas to digitize a flight-operations workflow that previously relied on more than 150 printed pages, manual logs, and rushed updates. The team modeled complex flight plans in MongoDB's document structure and used Atlas platform services to speed delivery of mobile synchronization, conflict resolution, permissions, security, and unreliable-network handling. Flight Folder stores data locally so pilots can work offline, then synchronizes changes back through the app and Atlas backend when connectivity returns. Dispatchers, crews, and refueling teams use the application to exchange updates in real time, while flight metrics such as fuel consumption and timestamps are sent to backend systems like OTP for immediate business analysis. The result is a zero-paper operating model that improves decision-making, turnaround time, and sustainability for mission-critical flights.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Hosts the backend data platform for Flight Folder and synchronizes operational flight data between crews, dispatchers, and downstream systems.

data_flow: Dispatchers publish flight plans and updates to Flight Folder, pilots read and record flight data locally even when offline, the app syncs back to MongoDB Atlas when connected, and backend systems such as OTP receive timestamps and operational metrics for immediate analysis.
business_outcome: Cathay Pacific digitized more than 340,000 flights, cut average ground time by eight minutes through digital refueling, reduced paperwork and emissions, and saved roughly HKD 100 million over five years.
metrics: Flight crews previously reviewed over 150 pages of printed text and charts for a long-haul flight.
Cathay Pacific launched one of the first zero paper flights in the world in September 2019.
Since launch, the company has flown more than 340,000 flights with full digital integration in the flight deck.
Digital refueling saves eight minutes of ground time on average.
The digitization of flight documents reduced the amount of paperwork by 50kg.
The improvements are estimated to have saved about 100 million HKD over five years and avoid 15,000 tons of carbon per year.
architecture_clues: Flight Folder supports offline data entry and later synchronization back to Atlas.
The application sends timestamps and fuel-consumption data to the OTP system in real time.
The same platform supports direct messaging between crews and refueling teams inside the app.
